method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); two regulative rules (the agency's progress updates every three months, s 59(3); the discloser's 28 days to apply for internal review, s 60(2)(a)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Public Interest Disclosures Act 2022 No 14 (NSW), corpus document nsw_legislation:2023-10-30/act-2022-014 from the Open Australian Legal Corpus (collected 10 March 2025; unofficial, possibly out of date), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2022-014.txt (text sha256 as recorded in act-2022-014.meta.json, 05414c3dea99a54577e7678307131e33e52d1a85ce69714e4abdc7ddc3e0dcbb)

seat: the discloser: the public official who makes, or is thinking of making, a disclosure about serious wrongdoing, and who may suffer detrimental action because of it (a witness, who need not be a public official, and any other person who suffers detrimental action ask the same questions)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run pid-dates.l4 ; l4 run pid-disclosures.l4 ; l4 run pid-protections.l4 ; l4 run pid-dealing.l4 ; l4 run pid-cases.l4
checks.result: 207 assertions written, 207 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-08)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read; a deliberately wrong assertion was checked to fail. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: In: ss 13, 14, 20 (key terms as they decide answers); Part 2 whole (ss 21-29); Part 3 whole (ss 30-41; s 34 as a comment); Part 5 ss 49, 59, 60, 61, 62, 64, 65 (ss 50, 55(3), 66 as facts or defences); s 7(2)(b). Out: ss 1-6, 8-12, 15-19 (machinery, or asked as facts), Part 4 (agency policies), ss 51-58 and 63 (agency handling), Part 6 (oversight), Part 7 (machinery; ss 84-85 offences in comments), Schedule 1 (transitional).
